primary_reason: Sportsbooks have PHI as a 6.0-point favorite, which works out to about a 69% chance to win. Clark also picks PHI.
secondary_reason: The game is at Lincoln Financial Field. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in Clark's model.
risk_factor: It's a division game. These teams play twice a year, and those games tend to be closer than expected. 11 mph wind: Moderate wind (11–20 mph): minimal impact; deep routes may be affected. Game-time temperature is around 40°F.
flip_scenarios: If PHI loses turnover margin by 2+, its win probability can collapse quickly.
If WAS converts its EPA edge into red-zone touchdowns, the model's lean can flip.

market_context.interpretation: Market inputs help calibrate baseline team strength, but football diagnosis sections intentionally avoid citing Vegas as the cause.

factor_cards.name: Market Edge
factor_cards.headline: The betting line favors PHI.
factor_cards.explanation: Sportsbooks have PHI as a 6.0-point favorite, which works out to about a 69% chance to win. Clark also picks PHI.

factor_cards.name: Home Field
factor_cards.headline: PHI are at home.
factor_cards.explanation: The game is at Lincoln Financial Field. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in Clark's model.

factor_cards.name: Momentum
factor_cards.headline: PHI have the better scoring margin.
factor_cards.explanation: Both teams are 3-0 over their last three, so the records are even. The difference is scoring margin: PHI have about 1 more point of scoring margin per game.
factor_cards.baseline_note: Last three: both 3-0; PHI +1 pt/gm scoring margin.

factor_cards.name: Recent Offense
factor_cards.headline: The offenses have been about even.
factor_cards.explanation: Over the last three games, PHI and WAS have gained about the same on a typical play, so offense isn't where this game gets decided.
factor_cards.baseline_note: Last 3 games, EPA/play edge: PHI -0.16; PHI offense +0.02 EPA/play (middle-of-the-pack).

factor_cards.name: Game Context
factor_cards.headline: Weather could matter.
factor_cards.explanation: It's a division game. These teams play twice a year, and those games tend to be closer than expected. 11 mph wind: Moderate wind (11–20 mph): minimal impact; deep routes may be affected. Game-time temperature is around 40°F.

factor_cards.name: Defensive Edge
factor_cards.headline: WAS's pass rush is the difference.
factor_cards.explanation: The two defenses have allowed about the same per play, but WAS have pressured the quarterback on 10% of dropbacks. Pressure like that disrupts J.Hurts and stalls drives.
factor_cards.baseline_note: EPA/play allowed edge, last 3: WAS -0.15; season: -0.05; WAS pressure rate 10%.

completed_games_only.rule: Only games before the predicted week are included in the training window.

no_future_leakage.training_rule: Train on seasons before 2024 plus 2024 weeks < 21.

learning_module.simple_explanation: Measures how much value a team creates every snap.
learning_module.why_predictive: Teams consistently generating positive EPA sustain offense better and do not need fluky field position.

model_meta.evaluation_method: Expanding-window weekly validation, trained on prior games and predicted forward
feature_categories: QB EPA per play (season + last 3 games)
model_meta.market_note: Vegas spread and moneyline are included as model inputs because they encode information the model can't fully capture from box-score stats alone. However, all explanations prioritize football factors over market signals.

current_season_ready_note: This version runs on historical backtest data. During a live season, the same pipeline refreshes weekly using current nflfastR/nflverse data - only games already played are used to build features.

football_factors.name: QB Efficiency
football_factors.reason: PHI's QB efficiency is meaningfully higher than KC's this season (0.196 EPA/play difference) - a gap that shapes drive consistency and big-play rate.

football_factors.name: Turnover Edge
football_factors.reason: PHI wins the turnover battle modestly - a 0.72 turnover-per-game edge that creates shorter fields and extra possessions.

football_factors.name: Offensive Efficiency
football_factors.reason: PHI's offense generates modestly more expected points per play than KC's (0.090 EPA/play difference), keeping drives alive and converting more consistently.

football_factors.name: Defensive Resistance
football_factors.reason: PHI's defense is slightly more stingy than KC's - allowing 0.028 fewer EPA per play and limiting opponent scoring opportunities.

football_factors.name: Pressure Matchup
football_factors.reason: KC wins the pass rush vs. protection battle slightly (0.024 sack-rate edge) - a mismatch that can collapse key third-down drives.
